d_stress.q: How much stress or pressure do you feel today?

d_motivation.q: How much do you want to train or compete today?

d_confidence.q: How sure do you feel today about what you can do in your sport?

d_focus.q: How clear is your head today for concentrating?

d_connection.q: How do you feel about your team and your people (teammates, staff, home)?

w_energy.q: I felt energetic and wanted to move.

w_tension_nerves.q: I felt nervous or tense thinking about training or matches.

w_tension_switch_off.q: I found it hard to switch off from competition, even when I wanted to rest.

w_mood_enjoy.q: I enjoyed the things I did, in and outside of sport.

w_irritability.q: I got angry or annoyed easily.

w_mental_fatigue.q: My head felt tired or overloaded.

w_confidence.q: I trusted my abilities in training and matches.

w_motivation.q: I wanted to improve and give my best.

w_pressure_perform.q: In important moments I was able to perform the way I know I can.

w_pressure_block.q: Pressure (results, coaches, family) froze me up.

w_resilience_reset.q: After a mistake I was able to leave it behind and stay focused.

w_resilience_dwell.q: I kept going over my mistakes for a long time.

w_cohesion.q: I felt part of the team and supported by my teammates.

w_balance_organize.q: I was able to fit sport around school, work or family.

w_balance_crowded.q: I felt sport left me no time for other things that matter to me.

talk.q: Would you like to talk to someone on the staff?
talk.hint: If you say yes, we let your club's medical staff know so they can reach out. You don't have to explain why.
talk.sent: We let your club's medical staff know: someone will reach out to you.

disclaimer.title: A wellbeing monitoring tool, not a clinical diagnosis.
disclaimer.body: Each athlete is compared only with themselves (their baseline), never with teammates. Scores summarise answers to short questions; they do not measure or label any condition.
disclaimer.referral: If you see warning signs, talk to the athlete and refer them to a mental health professional.

privacy.title: Who sees your answers?
privacy.body: Only your club's medical staff and administrators. Your coach sees at most a general heads-up (for example, that it would be good to check in with you), not your answers, unless the club has allowed it. They are never shared outside the club.
privacy.mood: Your mood (the first question) is saved with your wellness, as always, and your staff can see it.
privacy.noWrongAnswers: It's not a test: there are no right or wrong answers, and you can skip any question.
privacy.urgent: If you need help urgently, talk to a trusted adult now or call your country's emergency number.

portal.dailySubtitle: 6 quick questions (about 20 seconds). All of them are optional.
portal.weeklySubtitle: Optional, about 2 minutes. It helps you and your staff see how you are doing week by week.
portal.weeklyDoneDescription: We'll suggest the next one from {{date}}.

staff.title: Psychological wellbeing (entered on the athlete's behalf)
staff.subtitle: For answers the athlete gave on paper or during a consultation. Medical staff and administrators only.
staff.moodElsewhere: Overall mood is recorded in the wellness form.
staff.editingExisting: There is already a check-in for this athlete, date and type: saving will correct it.

sustained_decline.label: Sustained decline
sustained_decline.description: Mood or calm below their baseline on at least 3 of the last 5 days.

stress_spike.label: Stress spike
stress_spike.description: Stress at the top of the scale, or far above what is usual for this athlete, in the last 3 days.

wants_to_talk.label: Asked to talk to someone
wants_to_talk.description: The athlete asked to talk to someone on the staff in the last 7 days.

profile.lastCheckin: Last answer: {{date}} · {{n}} days with answers in 28 days
profile.flagsOnlyNote: You see a summary. Answers and scores are visible to the medical staff only.
profile.emptyDailyTitle: No daily check-ins in the last 28 days
profile.emptyDailyDescription: The athlete answers them in their portal together with wellness; the medical staff can also enter them.
profile.dailyRadarDescription: 0-100, 100 = most favourable state. Only dimensions with a baseline.
profile.buildingBaseline: Building their baseline: at least {{min}} answers in {{days}} days are needed to compare with what is usual for them.
profile.dailyTableDescription: Deviation = 7-day mean minus their baseline (previous 28 days). Trend = 7 days vs 28 days.
profile.scaleNote: 0-100 scale in the favourable direction: for calm, 100 = no stress at all. One step on the 1-5 answer scale equals 25 points.
profile.trendDescription: Last 28 days; the dashed line is their baseline.
profile.weeklyDescription: Last weekly check-in: {{date}} ({{n}} in the last 12 weeks)
profile.emptyWeeklyDescription: The portal suggests it to the athlete once a week; it is optional.

alerts.title: Psychological wellbeing
alerts.descriptionDetail: Athletes with signals in recent days, starting with anyone who asked to talk to someone.
alerts.descriptionFlags: Athletes worth checking in with. Answers are visible to the medical staff only.
alerts.empty: No wellbeing signals in recent days.

matrix.neverTooltip: The database never grants psychological wellbeing to this role, even if it is ticked here.
